what_happened: Claude Code updated itself from 2.1.299 to 2.1.301. This was the second automatic update in two days. Every agent then refused to start because the version no longer matched the pin in athena.toml. Repinning is normally done as a job, but no job could start, so the operator edited the pin by hand to follow Sri's standing instruction to update the pin. No job was involved, and the event is logged as an intervention.
cause: The pin check and the runtime's auto-update are not coordinated. Claude Code can change its own version at any time, but the pin only changes through a job, and a job needs a working agent. The repair path therefore depends on the thing that is broken. Nothing in Athena stops the self-update, notices the drift before agents start, or provides a repin path that works without an agent. The standing instruction to update the pin is a manual habit that repeats with each update, not a system behavior.
prevention: Two changes would prevent the whole class. First, turn off Claude Code's auto-update in the Athena environment (for example the DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER setting, or installing from a fixed location the updater cannot change), so the installed version only changes when Athena changes it. Second, add a code-level repin command that does not run through an agent job. It would detect an installed version that differs from the pin, check that the new version passes a smoke test, update athena.toml, and log the change as an event. This removes the deadlock, and the operator no longer edits the pin by hand.
proposed_request: Stop Claude Code from changing its own version under Athena, and make a version mismatch fixable without hand-editing. Outcomes: (1) The installed Claude Code version changes only when Athena changes it on purpose. Show this by running Athena across at least two days, or by simulating an available update, and confirming that the version and the pin still match. (2) If the installed version ever differs from the pin, Athena reports this clearly before any agent starts. It offers one operator command that repins to the installed version after a smoke test passes. The command does not need an agent job, and it records the change as a logged event with the old and new versions. (3) The current pin, 2.1.301, stays in force. Acceptance: with a deliberately mismatched version in a test environment, the command repins and a job can start afterward, and the repin appears in the event log.
